newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai government revenues rise 10 pct in Oct-Nov.
newsitem.headline: Thai government revenues rise 10 pct in Oct-Nov.

text.p: Thailand's finance ministry said on Friday that government revenue rose in the first two months of the 1997 fiscal year which began in October 1996.
Revenue rose by 10 percent to 114.45 billion baht ($4.58 billion) from the same period in the previous financial year.
Government spending in the same period rose 43.1 percent to 135.73 billion baht, a ministry statement said.
Tax collection by the Revenue Department in October and November totalled 68.75 billion baht, 13.32 percent higher than the amount collected in same year-ago period.
However, the tax collections in the period were 3.4 percent lower than that projected by the department, it said.

The Excise Department's revenue in October and November was 28.03 billion baht, or 10.81 percent higher than that collected in the same period a year ago, but 3.49 percent lower than projected, the ministry added.
The Thai parliament approved a record 984 billion baht budget for the 1997 financial year and the government said it would adopt a balanced budget policy this year. ($1 = 25.6 baht)
